validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: unambiguous — this is the East Mediterranean Gas (EMG) El-Arish–Ashkelon subsea line, one of the most heavily documented pipelines in the region (Kingston Corp transaction dossier, Washington Institute, WorldOil, Al Jazeera, Bloomberg, Reuters, Wikipedia Arab Gas Pipeline). Real. CLASSIFICATION: correct — international gas transmission trunk (subsea, ~85 km offshore), not gathering/feeder/oil. Correctly on the gas tracker. DUPLICATE: no GEM duplicate in the 50-row Egypt roster; the Arab Gas Pipeline rows (P0436 Arish→South Sinai, P7482 Taba→Aqaba) are the onshore AGP that this line branches from, not the same pipe. GulfPub carries the counterpart 'Ashkelon - Arish Pipeline | operating | Ashkelon, Israel -> Arish, Egypt | op=EMGC' — confirms existence/endpoints/operator, but its dia=16in / len=62km / start=2015 are ALL wrong vs the corroborated 26in / 90km / 2008; a clean example of GulfPub Tier-2 specs not being authoritative. SPEC CONFIRMATIONS (all >=2 independent): length 90 km (Kingston '89 km, of which 85.4 km subsea'; Wikipedia AGP '90 km'); capacity 7 bcm/y (Kingston '7-9 BCM per year'; Wikipedia '7 bcm/y physical, 9 with upgrades'); start 2008 (Kingston 'started operation May 2008'); stop 2012 (Kingston 'ceased operation in 2012' — sabotage of the Sinai feeder began 2011, contract formally revoked Apr 2012, GEM's 2012 is defensible); reverse-flow restart 2020 (WorldOil/Al Jazeera 15 Jan 2020, Tamar+Leviathan). OWNER: EMG 61% / EMED 39% is correct — the EMED JV (East Gas 50%, Delek 25%, Noble 25%) bought 39% of EMG in Nov 2019 for ~USD520m (Algemeiner, Washington Institute); operator remains EMG. CAVEAT: the row mixes eras — StartYear1=2008 is the original Egypt→Israel export start, but Location (Ashkelon→Arish) and status=operating reflect the post-2020 reverse import of Israeli gas to Egypt. Endpoints/direction as shown match current operation, so acceptable, but worth a one-line ResearcherNotes note. NOTE also a 2023-2024 Gaza-war interruption (flows suspended Oct 2023, rerouted via Jordan, later resumed) — status=operating still correct as of 2025.

validity.recommendation: Change FuelSource from 'Egypt' to 'Israel' (Tamar + Leviathan). The row's operating status reflects the post-2020 reverse flow importing Israeli gas INTO Egypt; the gas source is no longer Egyptian.
validity.researcher_notes: FuelSource=Egypt is stale/incorrect for the current operating reality. The line originally (2008-2012) carried EGYPTIAN gas to Israel, so FuelSource=Egypt was right for that era. But the row is marked operating on the basis of the 2020 reverse flow, which imports ISRAELI gas (from the offshore Tamar and Leviathan fields) into Egypt — corroborated independently by WorldOil (15 Jan 2020, 'supplies from its offshore Tamar field and the even larger Leviathan field'), Al Jazeera (15 Jan 2020), and the Washington Institute route analysis. Given the reversed Location (Ashkelon, Israel → Arish, Egypt) already in the row, FuelSource should be Israel to be internally consistent. If GEM wants to preserve the export-era history, note both eras in ResearcherNotes but set the live FuelSource to Israel.

waypoints.name: offshore Mediterranean corridor skirting west of the Gaza Strip (subsea, approximate — seabed path not published)

routes.corridor_desc: Predominantly subsea line (Kingston: 85.4 of 89 km offshore; WorldOil: 'runs mainly offshore, skirting the Gaza Strip'). From the Ashkelon coast (southern Israel) it runs south-southwest through Mediterranean waters, staying offshore past the Gaza Strip, to landfall at El-Arish on Egypt's North Sinai coast. Endpoints (Ashkelon, El-Arish) are high-confidence named cities/facilities; the exact seabed alignment between them is not public, so the intermediate corridor is bounded loosely to the near-shore eastern-Mediterranean strip between the two landfalls.
routes.researcher_notes: Endpoint coordinates are the well-known cities of Ashkelon (~31.669N, 34.572E) and El-Arish (~31.131N, 33.798E) — defensible from named places, not invented. Corridor established from Kingston (mostly subsea, ~85 km offshore) and WorldOil (skirts the Gaza Strip). No precise offshore waypoint coordinate is fabricated; the seabed path is described in prose only. Suggested medium accuracy reflects firm endpoints + a broadly-known but not surveyed offshore corridor.

summary: P0462 Arish–Ashkelon (EMG) real, correctly classified gas transmission trunk, no duplicate; specs (90 km, 7 bcm/y, 26in, 2008/2012/2020, EMG 61%/EMED 39%) all corroborated — one attribution concern: FuelSource=Egypt is stale, should be Israel under post-2020 reverse flow.
